parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR: Identify the error in this counterargument paragraph: 'Admittedly, some parents says smartphones helps children contact them in emergencies. However, this argument fail to consider that young children can use simpler devices for safety.'

2. STRUCTURE CHECK: Is this a counterargument paragraph? 'Some people think smartphones are educational. However, they are also very expensive. Furthermore, not all families can afford them.' → Is this a counterargument + refutation? Why/why not?
3. CAMBRIDGE PET: Write a 30-word concession + refutation using: 'Admittedly, [opposing view]... Nevertheless, [your argument with evidence]...'

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  THE 5-PARAGRAPH ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY
content: The classic argumentative essay has 5 paragraphs: Introduction (thesis), Body 1 (strongest argument), Body 2 (second argument), Body 3 (counterargument + refutation), Conclusion.
Notice that Paragraph 3 is a COUNTERARGUMENT PARAGRAPH. This is the advanced move that separates a good essay from a great one.
Sentence 1 (CONCEDE): 'Admittedly, / It is true that / Proponents of [opposite view] argue that [strongest opposing point].'
Sentence 2 (EVIDENCE FOR OPPOSITION): 'They support this claim with [evidence for opposing side].'
Sentence 5 (CONCLUSION OF REFUTATION): 'Therefore, while [opposing view] has some merit, [your position] is ultimately more supported by the evidence.'

listening_script.text:
The classic argumentative essay has 5 paragraphs: Introduction (thesis), Body 1 (strongest argument), Body 2 (second argument), Body 3 (counterargument + refutation), Conclusion.
Notice that Paragraph 3 is a COUNTERARGUMENT PARAGRAPH. This is the advanced move that separates a good essay from a great one.
STRUCTURE OF COUNTERARGUMENT PARAGRAPH:
Sentence 1 (CONCEDE): 'Admittedly, / It is true that / Proponents of [opposite view] argue that [strongest opposing point].'
Sentence 2 (EVIDENCE FOR OPPOSITION): 'They support this claim with [evidence for opposing side].'
Sentence 3 (TRANSITION): 'However, / Nevertheless, / Despite this,'
Sentence 4 (REFUTATION): '[Your strongest counter-evidence].'
Sentence 5 (CONCLUSION OF REFUTATION): 'Therefore, while [opposing view] has some merit, [your position] is ultimately more supported by the evidence.'
dictation: Notice that Paragraph 3 is a COUNTERARGUMENT PARAGRAPH.
This is the advanced move that separates a good essay from a great one.
